value.emollient_frequency: once daily, at least 3 hours after IP application, to untreated areas only
prohibited_concomitant: All other biologics (12 weeks or 5 half-lives)
Systemic antifungals, corticosteroids, immunosuppressive therapies, retinoids, roflumilast, or apremilast (Otezla)
Topical antifungals, corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, sulfur-based treatments, medical devices, crisaborole (Eucrisa), azelaic acid, or metronidazole
Medicated shampoos (e.g. coal tar, keratolytics including salicylic acid, antifungals, zinc pyrithione, selenium sulfide, corticosteroids, medical devices)
Topical medications used on the scalp for conditions besides seborrheic dermatitis (e.g. topical minoxidil for androgenetic alopecia)
Phototherapy, tanning beds, other light-emitting devices
Strong systemic P-450 cytochrome inhibitors (e.g. indinavir, nelfinavir, ritonavir, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nefazodone, saquinavir, suboxone, telithromycin)
permitted_concomitant: Non-medicated emollients, moisturizers and sunscreens, once daily as normally used, applied at least 3 hours after IP application to untreated areas only
Eye drop and nasal corticosteroid preparations
Inhaled corticosteroids if used for a stable condition at a stable dose for >28 days before screening and continued at the same dose throughout the study
Chronically used medications such as statins and anti-hypertensives

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 6.1.3. Multiple Comparisons: Secondary endpoints will only be tested if the primary endpoint is considered statistically significant at the alpha=0.01 level... the alpha level of 0.01 will be unequally split between two families of testing... The testing over the WI-NRS success endpoints and the other secondary efficacy endpoints will be sequential, utilizing the Fallback Method for unused alpha. For the testing of WI-NRS success endpoints, an alpha level of 0.0033 will be used and will use a hierarchical method to first test WI-NRS success at Week 8, followed by WI-NRS at Week 4, followed by WI-NRS success at Week 2... this unused alpha will be carried to the other secondary endpoint family, which would then be tested at the .0033+.0067=0.01 level... In the other secondary endpoint family, an alpha level of 0.0067... will be used to hierarchically test: 1) IGA Success at Week 4, 2) Scaling score of 0 at Week 8, 3) Erythema score of 0 at Week 8, 4) the percentage of subjects who attain IGA of 0 at Week 8, and lastly, 5) IGA Success at Week 2. ... all statistical tests will be conducted at the 0.01 significance level using 2-tailed tests.
